title: Nonlinear Functions, Part 1: The Idea and an Easy Problem

beats.say: Nonlinear functions are functions whose graphs are not straight lines. On the SAT, they are mostly quadratic functions, which make parabolas, and exponential functions, which grow or shrink by the same percent each period.

card.text: Graphs that are not straight lines

beats.say: You may also see higher-degree polynomials, such as cubics. You will evaluate these functions, find vertices and zeros, and interpret the numbers in a model.

card.text: Evaluate, find vertex and zeros, interpret

beats.say: Another common task is to choose the function that matches a description in words.

card.text: Match a function to a description

beats.say: A quadratic can be written in three different forms, and each form shows something different. Choose the form that answers the question.
The vertex of a parabola lies exactly halfway between its two zeros. This is useful when you know the zeros.
beats.item: The vertex is halfway between the zeros

beats.say: An exponential function multiplies by the same factor over equal intervals. Growth of r percent per period means a factor of one plus r, and decay means one minus r.
In f of t equals a times b to the t, the number a is the starting value, which is f of zero, and b is the factor per unit of t.
beats.item: f(t) = a·b^t: start a, factor b

beats.say: For a polynomial p, if p of c equals zero, then c is an x-intercept, and x minus c is a factor.
beats.item: Zero at c means (x − c) is a factor

scenes.title: Three forms of a quadratic
rows: zeros p and q; vertex at x = (p + q)/2

beats.say: In standard form, the constant c is the y-intercept, and the vertex has an x coordinate of negative b over two a.
In vertex form, you can read the vertex h comma k directly. Notice the minus sign inside the parentheses, so x plus three means h is negative three.
In factored form, the zeros are p and q, and the vertex has an x coordinate halfway between them.
If a is positive, the parabola opens upward, and the vertex is a minimum. If a is negative, it opens downward, and the vertex is a maximum.
For exponential models, use a times one plus r to the t for percent growth, a times one minus r to the t for decay, and a times two to the t over d for doubling every d units.
Easy example. For f of x equals negative x squared plus six x minus five, find f of negative one, and find the vertex of the graph.
Replace x with negative one. Keep the parentheses around negative one, because the square applies to the negative number first, and the minus sign in front comes after.
Negative one, squared, is positive one, and the minus sign in front makes it negative one. Six times negative one is negative six.
Add the three negative numbers. Negative one, negative six, and negative five add up to negative twelve.
The x coordinate of the vertex is negative b over two a. Here b is six, and a is negative one.
Two times negative one is negative two. Six over negative two is negative three, and the minus sign in front makes it positive three.
To find the y coordinate of the vertex, evaluate the function at x equals three.
Three squared is nine, with a minus sign in front. Six times three is eighteen.
Negative nine plus eighteen minus five is four. So the vertex is three comma four, and since a is negative, it is a maximum.
As a check, factor the function. It equals negative x minus one, times x minus five, so its zeros are one and five. Halfway between them is three, which matches the vertex.
To recap. Pick the quadratic form that answers the question, and remember that the vertex is halfway between the zeros.
beats.item: Pick the form that fits the question

beats.say: For exponentials, growth uses one plus r and decay uses one minus r, and a is the starting value.
Check the vertex using the zeros. In the next video, we work through a medium problem and a hard problem.
